system_description.narrative_title: War, Starlink & the Refining Boom: Geopolitics Reshaping Energy and Security
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative ties the Russia-Ukraine conflict (and related Middle East tensions) to a reshaping of global security, diplomacy and energy markets: battlefield communications (notably Starlink/SpaceX) are a strategic lever contested by states and private actors, while war-driven supply/demand shocks are producing record refining profits for major oil firms. Political interventions (calls between leaders and tech CEOs), regional courting by Russia, and divided Western responses are creating feedbacks between military operations, diplomatic negotiations and global commodity markets.
system_description.scope: Interactions among states (Russia, Ukraine, US, EU members, Turkey, regional partners), private firms (SpaceX, major oil & gas companies, defence suppliers), energy and commodity markets (refining, diesel supply), security operations (attacks, ceasefires, arms transfers), and diplomatic fora (G20, bilateral talks) over the 29–31 Oct 2026 news window.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system (international security, diplomacy, and commodity/value chains)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets & oil majors (refining margins, trade flows)
Technology and communications infrastructure (satcom, space-enabled battlefield connectivity)
International security & alliance networks (NATO/EU partnerships, regional militaries)
Diplomatic forums & crisis mediation (G20, peace talks, bilateral negotiations)

variables.name: Armed conflict intensity
variables.description: Measures the aggregate frequency, scale and lethality of kinetic military operations across relevant theatres.

variables.name: Battlefield communications availability
variables.description: Measures the operational availability and reliability of tactical communications networks supporting combat operations.

variables.name: Satellite communications dependency
variables.description: Measures the degree to which military and critical operations rely on space-based communications and relay services.

variables.name: Global refining margin level
variables.description: Measures the average per-barrel profit margin captured across global refining operations for refined fuels.

variables.name: Refinery capacity utilization
variables.description: Measures the proportion of installed refining capacity that is actively processing crude into products.

variables.name: Diesel supply balance
variables.description: Measures the net flow difference between diesel production/imports and consumption/demand over a rolling period.

variables.name: Refined product inventories
variables.description: Measures the aggregate stocks of refined fuels and related products held in commercial and strategic storage.

variables.name: Energy price volatility
variables.description: Measures short‑term variability and realized volatility in wholesale oil and refined fuel prices.

variables.name: Diplomatic cohesion
variables.description: Measures the degree of policy alignment and coordinated diplomatic action among relevant state coalitions.

variables.name: State–private coordination intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency and depth of operational coordination and information sharing between governments and private sector actors.

variables.name: Arms transfer rate
variables.description: Measures the rate and volume of international transfers of weapons, munitions and defense systems into conflict-relevant areas.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: Measures the intensity, scope and enforcement rigor of economic and trade restrictions applied to target actors.

variables.name: Electronic warfare capability
variables.description: Measures aggregate capability to conduct electronic, signals and related cyber-interference operations affecting communications and sensors.

variables.name: Maritime security tension
variables.description: Measures the level of hostile incidents, interdiction risk and navigational insecurity in strategic sea lanes and coastal zones.

variables.name: Political polarization in public discourse
variables.description: Measures the intensity of ideological division and antagonistic framing in public and elite discourse affecting policy options.

variables.name: Ceasefire probability
variables.description: Measures the evolving likelihood (as perceived and signalled) of local or broader ceasefires and pauses in hostilities.

catalysts.title: Zelenskiy travels to Turkey for talks
catalysts.description: High-level Ukraine diplomatic talks in Turkey led by Zelenskiy, potentially linked to ceasefire and security guarantee discussions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Zelenskiy says he will head to Turkey for talks' — could boost coordinated diplomacy and ceasefire prospects.

catalysts.title: Renewed strikes on Russian refineries
catalysts.description: Ukrainian attacks on Russian refining infrastructure continue in cycles, disrupting refinery operations and fuel flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Ending Pause...' and 'Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Russian Refineries After Pressure From U.S.' indicate resumed targeting.

catalysts.title: Change in Starlink restrictions / availability
catalysts.description: Political and private pressure leads to adjustments in SpaceX/Starlink policy and operational availability for Ukrainian military use.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump Called Musk...' and 'Ukraine’s Military Starlink Is Working Again' imply policy/availability shifts that affect dependency.

catalysts.title: Ongoing refining profit surge and capacity shifts
catalysts.description: Sustained record refining margins and producers maximizing diesel output drive higher utilization and margin dynamics across global refining.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple earnings headlines: 'refining margins soar', 'Shell maximizes diesel production', 'BP/Exxon/Chevron profits surge'.

catalysts.title: Sustained rise in arms transfers to hotspots
catalysts.description: Confirmed large sales and deliveries (Patriot, jets, air-defence) and bilateral deals increase weapons flows into conflict-relevant areas.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale', 'Ethiopia says it received Russian Su-35 jets', 'Germany to tap Ukrainian tech with missile purchase'.

catalysts.title: Increased electronic warfare deployments in Europe
catalysts.description: NATO/EU brigade deployments and EW units are being positioned to monitor/exert influence near Russia-border regions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Germany brigade in Lithuania to monitor Kaliningrad, Belarus with electronic warfare' indicates active EW posture increase.

catalysts.title: G20 friction over multiple wars
catalysts.description: Upcoming G20 meetings and foreign-minister-level actions expose rifts that could hinder collective diplomatic coordination on Ukraine and Middle East.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Rifts over wars in Ukraine, Middle East loom over G20 meeting' and 'G20 foreign ministers skip photo-op'.

catalysts.title: Executive withdrawals from ADIPEC / Gulf conference
catalysts.description: Major oil executives cancelling attendance at Gulf energy conference over security concerns, reducing near-term dealmaking and coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Exxon, Chevron cancel executive trips to UAE's ADIPEC' and 'ExxonMobil boss pulls out...security concerns'.

catalysts.title: Expansion of local humanitarian ceasefires
catalysts.description: Localized truces and relief pauses (e.g., Oleshky) may extend or be replicated, enabling limited humanitarian access and temporary calm.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia and Ukraine begin local ceasefire...' and 'US First Lady praised for Oleshky relief truce' show replicable local pauses.
